title: Wrong Enough
style: Electronic country, mid-tempo 4/4 with a clipped train-beat kick and snare, rubbery sub-bass under bright banjo-like plucks and steel-guitar bends. Start spare and observant; add tight electronic percussion and a pulsing synth bass through the verses, then open into a broad, hooky chorus with layered harmonies. Low, weathered male lead, conversational phrasing that turns wry and uneasy; crisp modern mix, dry close vocal, spacious guitar tails.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Challenger on the runway, Army green and brown
Canadian-built wings with the wrong coat painted on
Lines don't fit the fuselage, the badges sit askew
Fresh paint catching morning light where old wear ought to show through

[Pre-Chorus]
From the road it passes, official as a seal
But look a little closer and you feel what isn't real

[Chorus]
This is wrong on so many levels
Wrong paint, wrong place, wrong kind of crew
Dark jackets, DEA across the chest
No one pretending to be what they ain't
Perez waits inside, says, “Take it easy”
A faint smile, like he knows the joke
Close enough to fool the passing eye
Wrong enough to make the careful look twice

[Verse 2]
Carlson sees the seams before the engines even turn
A little too clean here, a little badge that doesn't earn
The men wear plain dark jackets, agency letters plain to see
That honest kind of mismatch feels stranger than a lie could be

[Pre-Chorus]
The paint says Army, but the crew says who they are
A borrowed look on a seized-up jet, dressed to travel far

[Chorus]
This is wrong on so many levels
Wrong paint, wrong place, wrong kind of crew
Dark jackets, DEA across the chest
No one pretending to be what they ain't
Perez waits inside, says, “Take it easy”
A faint smile, like he knows the joke
Close enough to fool the passing eye
Wrong enough to make the careful look twice

[Bridge]
“Two years ago, we took it from a narco down in Mexico
I wondered what the most dramatic use could be,” he says low
Now a witness rides beneath that freshly painted disguise
And Carlson reads the little errors no one else would recognize

[Final Chorus]
This is wrong on so many levels
Wrong paint, wrong place, wrong kind of crew
Dark jackets, DEA across the chest
Plain as day, and stranger for the truth
Perez waits inside, says, “Take it easy”
The engines stir the tarmac dust
Close enough to fool the passing eye
Wrong enough to make a careful man distrust

[Outro]
The badges sit a fraction off
The paint still looks too new
A jet dressed up to pass at distance
And Carlson sees it through
